name: Omaprox
author: AndresSM415
description: Read-only Proxmox VE dashboard in the Omarchy bar: every container and VM with a status LED, per-guest stats, and one key to a console.

barWidget.description: Browse every LXC and QEMU guest on a Proxmox VE cluster with a status LED per row, drill into one for CPU, memory, disk and network, and open a console — pct enter for containers, SSH for Linux VMs, xfreerdp3 for Windows. Nothing in the panel starts, stops or reconfigures a guest.

schema.label: Proxmox host
schema.description: Address of any node in the cluster, for example pve01.lan or https://10.0.20.2:8006. The scheme defaults to https and the port to 8006.

schema.label: API token file
schema.description: File holding the API token, kept out of shell.json so the secret is not in your config. Defaults to ~/.config/omaprox/token.

schema.label: Refresh interval (seconds)
schema.description: How often the guest list and node meters are re-read. Per-guest stats refresh at this rate too, but only for the guest on screen.

schema.label: Verify the TLS certificate
schema.description: Off by default because Proxmox ships a self-signed certificate. Turn this On once you have a real certificate, or point 'CA certificate' at your own CA.

schema.label: CA certificate
schema.description: PEM file for the CA that signed the Proxmox certificate. Setting this verifies the connection against it, whatever 'Verify the TLS certificate' says.

schema.label: SSH user for the node
schema.description: Used by the container console, which runs pct enter on the node the container lives on.

schema.label: SSH user for Linux VMs
schema.description: Used by the VM console, which connects to the guest itself rather than to its node.

schema.label: Windows username
schema.description: Pre-fills the username for Windows consoles so FreeRDP only asks for the password. Leave blank to be asked for both. There is no password setting on purpose — a password here would live in shell.json, and FreeRDP asks for it in the terminal instead.

schema.label: Container console command
schema.description: Runs in a floating terminal. Placeholders: {vmid} {name} {node} {address} {nodeUser} {guestUser}. Blank uses: ssh -t {nodeUser}@{node} pct enter {vmid}

schema.label: Linux VM console command
schema.description: Runs in a floating terminal. Same placeholders. Blank uses: ssh -t {guestUser}@{address}

schema.label: Windows VM console command
schema.description: Launched directly, not in a terminal. Same placeholders. Blank uses: xfreerdp3 /v:{address} /dynamic-resolution +clipboard

schema.label: Memory warning (%)
schema.description: A guest or node over this share of its memory gets a red LED and appears under Needs attention.

schema.label: List templates
schema.description: Templates are never running, so they are hidden by default and would otherwise fill the list with permanently dark LEDs.

schema.label: Read VM addresses from the guest agent
schema.description: Off by default: this is the one call that needs VM.Monitor rather than VM.Audit, so leaving it Off keeps the token strictly read-only. With it Off, a VM console falls back to the guest's name as a hostname.
